tob-4148: J. M. Rodwell’s 1861 rendering was the first to set the Qur’an’s surahs in time order, letting English readers track the Prophet’s message as it came. His clear Victorian prose served readers for generations. The version stands as a milestone in the West’s meeting with Islam’s scripture.
tob-0148: Farid ud-Din Attar’s Bird-Parliament is Persia’s great Sufi parable — thirty fowls fare through seven vales to find their king, the Simorgh, and find but themselves. Wrought about 1177, it stands among the crown-pieces of holy writ. The poem’s wit and ruth are not to be forgotten.
cia-0000102948: Released from CIA files, this 1983 intelligence report covers two subjects: how the Soviet Union used prison labor on large building projects like roads and dams, and a bidding contest involving the West German steel company Salzgitter. It shows how American analysts tracked Soviet forced labor and also watched Western business deals that could matter for security. A window into Cold War spying priorities.
cia-0000106148: An April 1994 memo from Oil Capital Limited listing the business ties of Roger Tamraz, a Lebanese-American oil financier known for big international energy deals. The memo itemizes his company affiliations, the kind of background check intelligence agencies keep on influential businessmen. It shows the CIA tracking money and influence in the global oil trade.
cia-0000108048: A June 1986 report on an MVD escort and patrol guard company, military unit 7461 — the Soviet Interior Ministry troops who guarded prisoners and camps. These were the men with the dogs and the watchtowers. The document shows the CIA documenting not just the camps but the machinery of men that kept them running.
cia-0000112348: A January 1993 report on a government ministry planning to study psychic powers and UFOs for future industry. Post-Soviet Russia entertained ideas the old regime would have suppressed — or secretly funded. The entry captures the freewheeling 1990s, when the line between science and speculation blurred.
cia-0000118648: A February 1968 situation appraisal assessing General Thang's performance as commander of South Vietnam's IV Corps in the Mekong Delta. American advisors graded allied generals the way teachers grade students — and the grades mattered for the war. The document is a report card from a war fought through proxies.
cia-0000119748: An October 1956 report on how Asia reacted to the Hungarian events. From Tokyo to New Delhi, governments and publics watched a small nation's bid for freedom — and its crushing. The document widens the lens: Hungary's tragedy as seen from the other side of the world.
cia-0000126948: A January 1991 terrorism review on the Mormon Church in South America as a terrorist target — the truncated title suggests the rest. American missionaries made conspicuous targets for anti-Yankee militants. The document shows terrorism's logic: attack the most visible Americans, even peaceful ones.
cia-0000132348: An October 1959 NSC briefing on the Sino-Soviet bloc's campaign in Latin America — the archive's spelling says Latiin. Moscow and Beijing were competing for the continent's revolutionaries. The document briefs the White House on the communist offensive in America's backyard.
cia-0000132448: A January 1960 report: Mikoyan in Cuba. The Soviet deputy premier's visit was the courtship made official — the USSR's number two, in Havana. The document records the moment the alliance went public: the embrace, photographed.
cia-0000132648: A May 1960 report: Mexico giving the visiting Cuban president a warm welcome. Mexico City embraced Havana even as others cooled — nationalism over alignment. The document is the welcome: the hosts, embracing.
cia-0000132748: A 1961 roundup of Cuban and Central American developments. The isthmus and the island, together. The document is the beat, covered: the developments, collected.
cia-0000134248: Item 12 in a 1960 series: pro-Castro activity in Peru. Lima's left was mobilizing for Havana. The document is the activity: the Peruvians, marching.
cia-0000136148: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting that WALDORF be interviewed. Someone needed questioning. The document is the request: the interview, ordered.
cia-0000136248: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN with a command message for CADICK on command authority established — the archive's punctuation stumbles, the truncated title cuts off by whom. The chain of command, settled. The entry is the authority: the command, established.
cia-0000136348: The final operations situation report, number 16, 1954. The last sitrep. The document is the finale: the operations, reported — for the last time.
cia-0000139048: A 1944 letter to the FBI requesting information on Gerhart Eisler. The wartime inquiry. The document is the request: the information, sought.
cia-0000139448: A 1986 DCI hostage location task force report — the archive's spelling says hostge. The hunt, continued. The entry is the report: the hostages, sought — through a typo.
un-ga-res-448: Resolution 448 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1950. The year the Korean War began — the Assembly's agenda turned to war and peace. The catalog records the number and year; the text records the act.
un-ga-res-48: UN General Assembly Resolution 48, from 1946. The first session's closing acts. The number and year survive; the decision belongs to the text.
un-ga-res-a-69-48: Resolution A/69/48, adopted in 2015 — the spillover year. The designation and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-248: Security Council Resolution 248, cataloged with the year 1967 — the numbering suggests 1968, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-648: Security Council Resolution 648, adopted in 1990 — aligned. The new decade's Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1348: Security Council Resolution 1348, adopted in 2001 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1648: Security Council Resolution 1648, adopted in 2005 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1848: Security Council Resolution 1848, adopted in 2008 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
plos-pone-0000048: A 2006 PLOS ONE study asking whether Factor XIII deficiency impairs wound healing after myocardial infarction — the truncated title cuts off the model. A clotting factor's role in healing heart attacks. The paper is the question: the healing, tested.
un-sc-res-1248: Security Council Resolution 1248, cataloged with the year 1248 — the year echoes the number, garbage; the real 1248 belongs to 1999. The designation is preserved; the date is not.
un-sc-res-848: Security Council Resolution 848, adopted in 1993 — aligned. The Council deciding. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
treaty-of-westphalia-1648: The Treaty of Westphalia of 1648 — here the Treaty of Münster — the settlement that ended the Thirty Years' War and invented the modern system of sovereign states. After a war that killed millions, Europe's rulers agreed that each prince would rule his own territory. The treaty is the settlement: the sovereignty, established.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d48: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 20, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 48. London wrote. The message is the letter: the prime minister, to the president.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d148: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 20, 1943 — Document 148. The president wrote Moscow. The message is the letter: the president, to the marshal.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d248: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 22, 1943 — Document 248. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the combined: the chiefs, Allied.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d348: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the minister in Egypt, Kirk — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 348. Another answer. The cable is the second: Hopkins, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d448: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 448. The connective passage. The note is the passage: the story, flowing.
arxiv-2605-08748: An entire function in complex analysis is defined smoothly over the whole complex plane, and a classic question asks when such a function is pinned down by the values it shares with its derivatives. Sujoy Majumder, Debabrata Pramanik, and Shantanu Panja prove uniqueness theorems for entire functions sharing two values with their partial derivative operators. The 2026 paper is pure mathematics in the value-distribution tradition.
arxiv-2605-08848: Ramsey theory asks how large a structure must grow before order inevitably appears; chi-bounds relate a graph's coloring number to the size of its largest clique. Tung H. Nguyen and Sang-il Oum prove Ramsey-type chi-bounds for chi-bounded graph classes, tightening the link between the two quantities. The 2026 paper is pure combinatorics.
arxiv-2605-08948: How strongly atoms hold onto each other decides whether a material is brittle or tough. Mateusz Mojsak, Elfi Kraka, and Adam A. L. Michalchuk compute bond strengths in solids from a Wannier-type construction of local vibrational modes — localized wiggles of the crystal. The 2026 paper is computational chemistry on the mechanics of materials.
arxiv-2605-09248: Galaxies clump together, and counting them correctly — accounting for the clustering — underpins cosmology. Yunting Wang, Ryley Hill, Douglas Scott, and Tessa Vernstrom explain how to count clustered galaxies. The 2026 paper is practical observational-cosmology methodology for surveys that map the clustered universe.
arxiv-2605-09348: Answering questions about your home — where is the spare key, is the oven on — needs knowledge graphs spanning text, images, and sensors. HOME-KGQA is a benchmark dataset for multimodal knowledge-graph question answering on household daily activities. The 2026 paper tests AI on domestic life.
plos-pone-0003448: Toxicologists tested a natural antidote to seafood poison in this 2008 study. Pacific ciguatoxin-1B, made by marine algae and concentrated in reef fish, triggers runaway nerve secretion. Brevenal, a compound from a related alga, blocked that toxic signaling in bovine nerve cells, hinting at a treatment for ciguatera poisoning, a common and miserable foodborne illness.
plos-pone-0003548: Vaccine researchers found a way around pre-existing immunity in this 2008 study. Many people already carry immunity to adenovirus 5, the carrier used in some vaccines, which blunts the shot's effect. Delivering the vaccine through the nose bypassed that interference and improved immune responses, a practical route for adenovirus-based vaccines.
plos-pone-0003648: In 2008, a team linked oxygen loss at birth to later brain changes in rats. Pups starved of oxygen grew fewer dentate granule cells, memory-related neurons, and as adults they ran about far more on methamphetamine. The work models how a rough start at birth can tilt the brain toward traits seen in serious mental illness.
plos-pone-0003748: In 2008, Pereira, Empadinhas, and Albuquerque solved a TB enzyme's structure. The glucosyl-3-phosphoglycerate synthase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis builds a sugar key to the bacterium's survival chemistry. The atomic structure hands drug designers a concrete target in the fight against resistant TB.
plos-pone-0003848: A 2008 cell biology study mapped a vessel-growth control circuit. Signaling through VEGF receptor-2, which drives both normal development and tumor blood supply, was found to depend on the IQGAP1 pathway for endothelial cell growth. The result names a control point in the vessel-building machinery that cancers hijack.
plos-pone-0003948: In 2008, Wallach, Ashash, and Michael took a chicken vaccine to the farm. Their subunit vaccine against Eimeria parasites, which cause costly coccidiosis, was tested in field conditions. The real-world trial moves poultry protection from lab to coop.
plos-pone-0004048: In 2008, Gingras, Lariviere, and Macaluso asked how age shapes scientific output. They tracked publication and citation patterns across researchers' whole careers. Older scientists published differently, leaving distinctly shifting citation footprints. The findings speak to heated debates about grant age and scientific renewal.
plos-pone-0004148: In 2009, Bonadonna, Caro, and Brooke found seabirds smelling sex. Antarctic prions recognized mates' sex by scent alone. Chemical signals, long ignored in birds, proved informative. The nose joins the bird's social toolkit. The finding widens the known senses of seabird courtship.
plos-pone-0004248: In 2009, Sowa, Vadakkan, and Zylka found a pain enzyme with a pH switch. Mouse PAP showed pH-dependent ectonucleotidase activity through adenosine receptors. The pain-pathway enzyme's output tracked acidity. The switch suggests pH-tuned pain drugs. The work points to gentler, targeted pain relief.
plos-pone-0004348: In 2009, Foley, Yeh, and Maeder built better gene scissors. Custom zinc finger nucleases made by oligomerized pool engineering mutated zebrafish genes fast. The OPEN method sped genome editing. The tool predates CRISPR's rise. The work laid groundwork for modern gene editing.
plos-pone-0358648: Entrepreneurship courses promise real-world skills — but what actually produces integrated learning? Drawing on student perceptions, this paper traced pathways to integrated learning outcomes in professional and entrepreneurship education. The evidence points to which teaching designs fuse knowledge, skills, and mindset.
plos-pone-0358348: Investor mood moves markets — and smart portfolios can exploit it. This study wove investor sentiment into stock portfolio construction using the Black-Litterman model. The sentiment-aware portfolios aim to ride the crowd’s emotions profitably rather than being blindsided by them.
plos-pone-0357448: Aligning medical images is brutally hard when anatomy varies between patients. This anatomy-aware, label-informed approach improves image registration for challenging datasets. The method aligns scans more faithfully by actually understanding the structures it’s matching — not just the pixels.
plos-pone-0356748: Getting to a doctor in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, depends heavily on where you live. This geographic information systems-based analysis mapped accessibility to medical institutions across the prefecture. The spatial analysis exposes healthcare deserts hiding inside a wealthy region.
plos-pone-0357048: Floods drown rice — unless the variety can hold its breath. This phenotypic evaluation tested local rice landraces for tolerance to submergence stress. The resilient landraces it identified are genetic treasures for breeding flood-proof rice.
plos-pone-0346348: Training health workers to seize ‘teachable moments’ for behavior change sounds simple — but what actually works, for whom, and when? This mixed-methods realist evaluation investigated exactly that for opportunistic behaviour change conversations. The nuanced findings move beyond ‘does it work’ to ‘how, for whom, and why.’
plos-pone-0354348: Magnetic slurries — Fe3O4 suspensions — change viscosity over time in ways engineers must predict. This paper studied the viscosity time-varying law and the microscopic chain-forming mechanism behind it. The findings help designers harness these smart fluids for dampers, seals, and precision devices.
plos-pone-0356548: Has Western classical music grown more novel or more harmonious over the centuries? This paper quantified the evolution of harmony and novelty across the canon. The computational musicology reveals the long arc of musical change — and punctures some cherished myths about it.
plos-pone-0355048: Managing snapper-grouper fisheries means juggling dozens of species at once. This paper navigated that complexity, evaluating management measures for multispecies fisheries in the Southeast U.S. Atlantic. The evaluation reveals which regulations actually sustain both fish populations and fishing livelihoods.
plos-pone-0355948: Bacterial vaginosis in pregnancy threatens both mother and baby — and diagnosis methods disagree. This paper associated BV prevalence with maternal characteristics while diagnostically comparing the BV Rapid Blue test against Amsel’s criteria. The head-to-head comparison guides obstetricians toward the more reliable diagnosis.
plos-pone-0356148: Quitting smoking may reprogram the cellular neighborhood around precancerous lung nodules. This mouse study examined smoking cessation’s regulatory effects on the cellular microenvironment and differentially expressed genes in precancerous lesions. The findings reveal that quitting doesn’t just stop damage — it actively remodels tissue toward health.
plos-pone-0355548: Alzheimer’s disease and HIV encephalitis — seemingly unrelated — may share molecular machinery. This paper unraveled their nexus through cellular senescence and transcriptional regulation. The shared mechanisms suggest therapies for one brain disease might help the other — a provocative convergence.
plos-pone-0351948: Psammophilic — sand-loving — scarab beetles radiated across ancient dunes. This phylogeography of Geopsammodius traced that radiation of endemic beetles. The evolutionary history reveals how life diversifies in Earth’s most shifting habitats.
plos-pone-0355848: Heart failure patients who develop acute infections face a frailty tipping point — and common diuretics might influence it. This paper examined frailty prediction in these patients, probing thiazide diuretics’ potential role. The findings suggest a familiar drug might modulate vulnerability when infection strikes a failing heart.
plos-pone-0354748: Norm-driven decisions — following social rules — involve regret, uncertainty, and limited rationality. This paper explored those intertwined forces. The theoretical analysis reveals why people follow norms even when the math says otherwise — and what that means for designing institutions that work with human nature rather than against it.
europmc-pmc2811148: Genome-wide association studies link common DNA variants to diseases, but this 2010 paper sounds a cautionary note. The authors show that rare variants can team up to create fake signals at common variants, producing synthetic associations. The finding means some reported gene-disease links may point to the wrong culprit. It changed how geneticists interpret association results.
europmc-pmc2848648: Spotting genes in germ DNA is code-breaking work, and this 2010 paper hands the trade a sharp tool. The authors bring Prodigal, which spots germ genes and their start flags. They prove it tops old code. Prodigal turned standard as germ-book first pass.
europmc-pmc2852848: Olive oil's fame may rest on its bitter parts. This 2010 review sifts what virgin olive oil's phenol compounds do in the body, from cell defense to heart effects. The authors weigh proof of gain against hype across many studies. Their take backs the oil's halo with care, while noting where proof runs thin.
europmc-pmc2859048: A rare blood disorder turns deadly when a key enzyme runs out. This 2010 paper hunts warning signs of severe ADAMTS13 loss in patients with thrombotic microangiopathies, drawing on France's referral center. The authors' list aids fast calls. Their work helps doctors spot the worst cases sooner.
europmc-pmc2898848: Bug sprays are everywhere, including inside people. This 2010 paper gauges breakdown bits of pyrethroid sprays in urine from everyday Americans, using national survey data from 1999 to 2002. The authors show contact is wide across ages and regions. Their baseline feeds ongoing risk debates about these common chemicals.
europmc-pmc2908548: RNA viruses travel as swarms of mutants, not single strains. This 2010 review explains quasispecies theory and how it governs RNA virus behavior. The authors show why the swarm, not the individual, is the unit of selection. Their overview reshaped thinking about viral evolution and drug resistance.
europmc-pmc2920848: The cell's power-plant DNA was a diabetes suspect, but this 2010 paper clears it. The authors find common hand-me-down tweaks in these genes do not track with type 2 diabetes or sugar traits. Their null result sent hunters elsewhere.
europmc-pmc2936548: Flu viruses hijack a cell-surface receptor to slip inside. This 2010 paper shows the epidermal growth factor receptor helps pull influenza A viruses into host cells. The authors expose the doorway the virus uses. Their finding suggests blocking entry as defense.
europmc-pmc2946948: A flipped chromosome chunk can remake a species' way of life. This 2010 paper shows a widespread inversion polymorphism drives a major life-history shift, local adaptation, and reproductive isolation. The authors catch evolution's lever in the wild. Their work is a textbook case.
europmc-pmc2965748: Old germ-killing molecules might become tomorrow's drugs. This 2010 review asks if natural germ-fighting peptides can serve as new medicines. The authors weigh ancient defenses for modern use. Their overview bridges evolution and the drug shelf. Bacteria find these hard to outwit.
europmc-pmc2992548: Disease mutations need 3D context, and this 2010 paper delivers it. The authors build a web tool that maps disease mutations onto protein shapes. Their tool brings structure to bench scientists. The work opened structural biology to all. Doctors check it before judging a variant.
europmc-pmc2996748: Fitting drugs into protein pockets is hard. This 2010 review surveys protein-ligand docking: its wins and its stuck points. The authors guide computer-aided drug hunters. Their review shaped the field. Better scoring functions remain the holy grail. The review still anchors methods courses.
europmc-pmc3041648: Disease counters got free software. This 2011 paper updates WINPEPI, a free toolkit for epidemiologists and teachers. The author's programs spread through classrooms. Their work trained a generation. Students run real outbreak math on it. The toolkit needs no license or fees.
europmc-pmc3080848: Motivation splits into parts. This 2011 paper teases apart drive, energy, and liking in learned behavior. The authors reveal the three strands. Their work lights up decision science. Depression dulls each strand differently. Drugs of abuse hijack the drive strand. Therapists target the strands separately.
europmc-pmc3100248: Healing bubbles got a factory. This 2011 paper scales up production of therapeutic exosomes from engineered stem cells. The authors' process powers mass production. Their work points to clinical bubble drugs. Heart-attack trials use the bubbles. The factory runs in sterile bioreactors.
europmc-pmc6551848: Do adults remember childhood maltreatment the same way records captured it at the time? This meta-analysis compared prospective measures (recorded during childhood) with retrospective ones (recalled as adults) - and found they often disagree. The mismatch matters: the two methods may identify different people, shaking assumptions behind much trauma research.
europmc-pmc6617248: Alzheimer's drug development is a graveyard of failed trials - so where is the pipeline headed? This 2019 census counts every drug in testing, what targets they chase, and how trial designs are evolving. The snapshot helps the field learn from failures and aim the next wave smarter.
europmc-pmc6636548: The 'neonatal Fc receptor' is badly named - it works far beyond newborns and Fc fragments. This review asks whether FcRn deserves its title, touring its real jobs: recycling antibodies to extend their life and ferrying them across barriers. The misnomer stuck, but the biology is richer than the name suggests.
europmc-pmc6688448: When people watch the same film, their brains dance in sync - and that synchrony can be measured. Intersubject correlation uses one person's brain activity to predict another's, revealing shared responses even without button presses. The method opens natural, movie-like experiments to rigorous brain science.
europmc-pmc6708248: Every tumor carries unique mutations - and some spell out targets found nowhere else in the body. Neoantigen vaccines train the immune system on these tumor-only flags, an emerging form of personalized immunotherapy. This review covers the young field's science and its promise for cancers that dodge standard care.
europmc-pmc6754748: Autism is one label for a thousand different profiles. This review argues big data can unpack the spectrum's heterogeneity: layering genetics, brain imaging, and behavior to find meaningful subgroups. The data-driven approach promises care matched to the person, not the label.
openalex-w7204987148: In 2025, the Brazilian state of Paraiba logged 7,122 poisoning cases, and this study profiles the ones caused by medicines. The authors break down who was poisoned, by which drugs, and in what settings, using plain case counts. The numbers show patterns, accidental, on purpose, and work-related, that point to ways of stopping future cases. A fact-based snapshot of a quiet public-health problem.
openalex-w7204991548: Blood pressure often drops during surgery, and kidneys are among the first organs to suffer. This study examines how the depth and duration of intraoperative hypotension affect the risk of acute kidney injury after operations. The authors analyze the link between low blood pressure on the table and kidney outcomes in recovery. A precise clinical investigation with a direct message for anesthesiologists: pressure matters, and minutes count.
openalex-w7205000548: College pressure drives some students to study drugs like lisdexamfetamine and methylphenidate, hoping for better grades. This paper reviews the risks of that misuse: health harms, dependence, and the false promise of smarter performance. The authors focus on why high-achieving students reach for pills and what it costs them. A cautionary review aimed at campuses where the medicine cabinet doubles as a study aid.
openalex-w7204448948: Artificial intelligence is entering biology classrooms, promising new tools and raising new worries. This paper reviews the potential and the pitfalls of AI in teaching biological sciences: what it can do for learning, and the teaching, ethical, and academic challenges it brings. The authors aim for balance over hype. A timely guide for biology teachers facing the AI question.
openalex-w7204260448: Energy drinks promise focus but may frazzle the brain. This integrative review studies what the science says about these beverages' effects on the central nervous system. The authors screened Portuguese and English research from 2021 to mid-2025. A timely review of the can behind the buzz.
openalex-w7128707048: Robots are entering the chest surgeon's toolkit. This paper reports Juntendo University's experience with robot-assisted lung cancer surgery since 2017: safety and benefits. The authors tracked the program's growth past 15 percent of cases. A surgical report from the robotic frontier.
openalex-w7214311248: Undoing an ileostomy can leave a hernia where the stoma was. This study of 194 patients hunted risk factors for these hernias, with focus on what thread closed the muscle layer. The team counted how often they struck. A surgery study of closing bellies cleanly.
pmc-13446148: A 2026 study of people with knee osteoarthritis linking pain sensitivity profiles — how individuals respond to standardized pain tests — to muscle biomechanics and real clinical pain. The connection between lab-measured sensitivity and lived pain helps explain why the same joint damage hurts some more than others. It moves pain medicine toward personalization.
pmc-13445148: This 2026 exploratory study asked whether social relationships affect experimental pain sensitivity in healthy teenage girls. Early evidence suggests social connection shapes how pain is processed even in adolescence. The preliminary findings open a window on the social side of pain biology.
pmc-13443148: This 2026 review traces the Warburg effect — cancer's preference for sugar fermentation over efficient energy production — in gastric cancer, from molecular mechanisms to targeted therapy. The authors show how an old observation is yielding new drug targets. It connects a century of metabolism research to today's stomach cancer treatment.
pmc-13442048: A 2026 theoretical chemistry paper developing a family of non-bivariational time-dependent coupled-cluster methods for simulating mixtures of fermions — particles like electrons — over time. These quantum methods aim for accuracy without crushing computational cost. The work gives physicists sharper tools for modeling ultrafast molecular dynamics.
pmc-13446548: This 2026 ophthalmology study followed sleep apnea patients for seven years to see how CPAP treatment affects the retinal vasculature. The eye's blood vessels mirror the body's, so retinal changes reflect systemic vascular health. Long follow-up like this shows whether treatment protects the small vessels.
pmc-13426048: This 2026 review presents keratan sulfate — a sugar chain found in cartilage and cornea — as an electroconductive glycosaminoglycan sitting at the interface of sensory perception and neural signaling. The idea that these molecules conduct electrical signals reframes their role. The paper gathers the evidence for a provocative hypothesis.
pmc-13459548: A 2026 paper offering a molecular solution to the paradox of ancient brain preservation — how brains survive in the archaeological record when soft tissue shouldn't. The chemistry of preservation turns out to explain it. The study resolves a long-standing puzzle.
pmc-13476248: A 2026 computer vision paper on a frequency-saliency guided multi-scale feature fusion network for robust UAV object detection. Drones need reliable vision. The network architecture is the contribution.
pmc-13469248: A 2026 study of allostatic load profiles — cumulative wear from stress — resilience, and psychosocial adaptation in young adults. The body's stress burden shapes mental health. The profiles reveal who's coping and who isn't.
pmc-13424448: In this 2026 nephrology paper, the spectrum of HIV-associated kidney pathology at a South African tertiary center was described. The pathology patterns inform regional care. The spectrum is the contribution.
pmc-13422848: This 2026 perspective touted the promise of deep urine proteomics for diagnosing cancer, neurologic, and metabolic diseases. Urine proteins could become a diagnostic goldmine. The paper makes the case.
pmc-13530548: This 2026 conference poster pitted bot against doctor at reading proximal humerus fracture X-rays. The AI challenge was playful but serious. The poster reports who won.
pmc-13512748: This 2026 machine learning paper introduced adaptive momentum Langevin dynamics for efficient posterior sampling. The sampler accelerated Bayesian inference. The dynamics are the innovation.
pmc-13545748: A 2026 sub-study of the FET optimizing trial on luteal phase progesterone support's effect on thyroid function. The fertility treatment's thyroid impact was measured. The sub-study is the detail.
pmc-13488448: In this 2026 evolution paper, evolutionary convergence on a dihydrofolate reductase mutation drove trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole resistance in Burkholderia thailandensis. The same mutation evolved repeatedly. The convergence is the warning.
pmc-13472948: In this 2026 plant pathology paper, a rare recombination in the Phytophthora sojae genome allowed redefinition of a major avirulence gene. The soybean pathogen's genetics were clarified. The recombination is the key.
pmc-13424748: A 2026 paper showing miR-125b-5p promoted pemphigus vulgaris pathogenesis by modulating desmosome structures. The microRNA disrupted the skin's anchors. The modulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13459948: A 2026 study of leisure-time physical activity and metabolomic trajectories over the transition from late midlife to old age. The exercisers' metabolites were tracked. The trajectories are the aging biology.
pmc-13251348: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical and sociodemographic correlates of poor medication adherence in bipolar disorder. The adherence barriers were pooled. The correlates guide intervention.
pmc-13439948: A 2026 paper: compound effector genes suppressed malaria parasite infections in gene-drive population modification strains of African malaria mosquitoes (the title is truncated). The engineered mosquitoes resisted the parasite. The suppression is the malaria control hope.
pmc-13526848: A 2026 materials paper: horizontally arranged covalent organic framework nanowires on poly(amidoxime) fibers for high-efficiency uranium capture. The uranium harvesters were engineered. The capture is the environmental advance.
pmc-13474148: In this 2026 obesity paper, GLP-1 and peptide YY multi-agonism with GEP44 optimized weight loss and glycemic control while reducing gastrointestinal side effects (the title is truncated). The multi-agonist was the advance. The optimizing is the therapeutic win.
pmc-13582148: In this 2026 cardiology paper, an intravascular ultrasound-derived calcium score predicted stent underexpansion in moderately to severely calcified lesions. The calcium score forecasted the stent failure. The predicting guides intervention.
pmc-13624248: A 2026 real-world study of filgotinib in moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis — up to 6-month effectiveness, patient-reported outcomes, and persistence. The JAK inhibitor's real-world performance was measured. The study informs rheumatology.
pmc-13545448: A 2026 paper on AI-assisted clinical exome sequencing — insights and outcomes from 822 pediatric diagnoses. The AI-aided sequencing diagnosed the children. The outcomes are the evidence.
pmc-13473448: A 2026 shoulder surgery paper on clinical outcomes of modified Kessler tension-reducing suturing combined with double-row repair for Patte II–III rotator cuff tears. The suture technique's results were reported. The outcomes are the evidence.
pmc-13428448: This 2026 nationwide cohort study examined age-stratified risk of major systemic complications following unicompartmental versus total knee arthroplasty. The partial-versus-total knee risks were compared by age. The risk data guide surgical choice.
pmc-13539948: In this 2026 tomato paper, domestication-associated reduction of methyl salicylate in roots was linked to root-knot nematode resistance. The breeding trade-off was decoded. The reduction is the evolutionary story.
pmc-13571348: This 2026 case report described OFDI-guided stentless PCI for erosion-related STEMI unmasking antiphospholipid syndrome. The imaging-guided intervention revealed the clotting disorder. The case is the cardiology lesson.
pmc-13418048: This 2026 neuroscience paper mapped an anterior cingulate-anterior insular glutamatergic circuit gating stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity and anxiety via ionotropic glutamate receptors (the title is truncated). The brain-gut circuit was decoded. The gating is the mechanism.
arxiv-2606-16148: This chip paper has a twin: the AIA speed story. Its tricks: a smart way to draw dice-roll numbers (Knuth–Yao rolls) and cores that share scratch space to cut data hauls. Both speed up quick-guess math — the good-enough sums behind much of AI.
arxiv-2606-16248: Sky pros read the past by fitting sky math to sky facts — by hand math, by quick-guess math, or by full fake-sky runs. This paper lines up all three ways on late-era cosmos data and grades which to trust, when. A buyer's guide for cosmos fitters.
arxiv-2606-16548: Fractional quantum Hall states are among the most exotic phases of matter. This paper gives recipes for preparing them on quantum computers — step-by-step circuits that build these delicate states qubit by qubit. It targets quantum computing researchers who want to simulate topological matter on real hardware.
arxiv-2606-16648: Blocking sunlight with giant space shades is a proposed climate intervention, but getting a huge shade into orbit is the hard part. This paper presents a conceptual sunshade design with an origami-inspired folding strategy — packing a vast reflector into a rocket fairing. It targets space engineers studying solar geoengineering concepts.
arxiv-2606-16748: Computer-use agents click and type like humans — but do they adapt to YOUR machine? MyPCBench tests 'personally intelligent' computer-use agents: ones that learn your files, apps, and habits. It is for researchers building truly personal AI helpers. One bench, many desks.
